The core mathematical insight is that human decision-making under uncertainty operates within bounded rationality: we cannot perfectly map an infinite state space onto a finite mental model. This leads to four key failure modes: (1) Overfitting to training data (fixed playbook), (2) Information-theoretic bottlenecks limiting anticipation horizon, (3) Catastrophic policy fragility to small environmental changes, and (4) Self-fulfilling prophecy of agent degradation when autonomy is suppressed. These primitives form a unified lattice of constraint, where each node represents a different facet of the same fundamental limitation: the impossibility of achieving omniscient control in stochastic environments. In GSI, this maps to static betting lines as insufficient priors; in GSE, it manifests as rigid state machines failing to capture emergent dynamics.
